# Systems concepts
## Caching
A cache stores copies of data so that later requests can use a faster storage layer. A cache hit finds the requested data there; a cache miss must obtain it elsewhere. A cache can return stale data if changes are not invalidated. A higher hit rate does not by itself guarantee correctness.
## Latency and throughput
Latency is the time needed for one operation. Throughput is the number of operations completed per unit of time. More parallel workers can improve throughput without reducing one operation's latency.
## Deadlock
Deadlock is a situation in which tasks wait indefinitely for resources held by one another. Circular waiting can produce deadlock. A long-running task alone is not necessarily a deadlock.
## Atomicity
An atomic transaction either commits all of its changes or leaves none of them applied. Atomicity is not the same as a transaction's isolation from concurrent work.
## Networking
TCP provides an ordered byte stream and retransmits lost data. UDP sends independent datagrams without that transport-level guarantee. An application can build reliability on top of UDP. Neither protocol alone encrypts application content.

# Motion and measurement
## Speed and velocity
Average speed is total distance travelled divided by elapsed time. Average velocity is displacement divided by elapsed time. Distance is a scalar path length, whereas displacement is a vector from the initial position to the final position. A runner returning to the start has zero displacement but may have travelled a positive distance.
## Acceleration
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. An object can accelerate at constant speed when its direction changes. Speed alone cannot establish whether acceleration is zero.
## Units
Speed has units of metres per second, written m/s. Acceleration has units m/s squared. A graph's slope is a change in its vertical quantity divided by a change in its horizontal quantity.
## Kinetic energy
For an object of mass m moving at speed v in the nonrelativistic regime, kinetic energy is one half of m times v squared. Doubling the speed at fixed mass multiplies this energy by four.

# Lab handbook — issued 3 October 2026
This handbook replaces the archived September instructions for Report B2.
## Report B2
Report B2 requires 2200 words excluding appendices. Submit a PDF by 2 December 2026 at 16:00 UTC. It is worth 30 percent of the module grade. The deadline is stated in UTC, not in the learner's local timezone.
## Experiment E4
The optional E4 reflection suggests 900 words. It is ungraded. Its suggested length and status do not apply to Report B2.
## Absence
A missed laboratory requires a make-up session only when the teaching office approves it. Sending a request does not itself grant permission. This handbook gives no automatic attendance exemption.
## Equipment
Laser demonstrations must be supervised by the instructor. Students may analyse the provided measurements independently, but they may not operate the laser alone.
## Not announced
The handbook does not announce the final exam's room, start time or duration. Study groups may use 20-minute revision blocks; these are not exam timings.
